method: Flesch-Kincaid grade with a transparent vowel-group syllable heuristic; estimated age = grade + 5, floored at zero. Count sentences using terminal punctuation. Exact measured corpora included. This is a rough editorial screen, not a learner assessment. Teacher-only text excluded.

corpora.text: I can choose a voice and a move for a made-up role. I can try two ways to say a line. I can choose one small move. I can show my choice and why. Pick a role: Keeper or Helper. You can sit, point, speak, sign or direct. This is a made-up story. Hear: My table has moved. Hear it fast. Hear it slow. Point: fast or slow? Watch the two Keeper versions. Hear one line in two ways. Watch one small hand move. Which way might you choose? Choose fast or slow for our Keeper. Choose one small move. Try the line and move once. Say: We chose ___ because ___. In your book or arts log, pick a role. Try the line fast, then slow. Try a small move with the line. Keep one voice and one move. Say or show why. Show your line and move, or direct it. A partner says: I notice ___. Tell us your choice. Put your work in a safe place. Arts log: My role is ___. I tried fast and slow words. I chose ___ and ___ because ___. Next time I will ___. The part you play in a story. The sound you use to say words. How fast you speak or move. A short stop.

Pick Keeper or Helper. Tell the adult: fast or slow. Choose an open hand or still hands. Try both ways. Keep one. Say or show why. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Pick your role and line. Try fast and slow words. Add one small move or pause. Keep a voice and move. Log your reason. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Do the same core task. Change the pause or one hand move. Say how the new choice changes the role. Keep a note of both real tries. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

The Keeper says, "My table has moved." The words come fast. The hands stop by the chest. The Keeper then asks, "Can you help?" Are the first words fast or slow? What small hand move did the Keeper use? The Keeper says the same words slowly. One open hand points to an empty spot. There is a short pause. The Keeper then asks, "Can you help?" What has changed in this version? Which version fits your Keeper? Why? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Say the Keeper line quickly at quiet talking level. Keep hands by the chest. Say the same line slowly. Open one hand towards an empty spot. Say: I choose slow words because my Keeper looks first. Show a short pause. Ask pupils to choose fast or slow and perform their choice once. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Develop a character with voice and movement. I can try two ways to say a line. I can choose one small move. I can show my choice and why. role: The part you play in a story. voice: The sound you use to say words. pace: How fast you speak or move. pause: A short stop. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can use my voice and move in a short scene. I can use my chosen voice and move. I can try one helpful change. I can log what I kept and why. Find your real choice note. Pick act, speak, sign or direct. We use the same made-up story. Try your line and move once. A partner watches or listens. Say: I notice ___. Watch our three-line scene. Keeper: My table has moved. Helper: We can find a new spot. Keeper: I will try that. Hear a pause. See a small move. Pick Keeper or Helper. Use a hand cue for each turn. Try the three lines together. Choose one part to make clear. Use your voice and move in the scene. Try it once with your partner or adult. Hear: I notice ___. Change one part if it helps. Try it again. Keep your choice. Show a short part or direct it. Listener: I notice ___. Maker: I kept ___ because ___. Store the real log. My role was ___. I used ___ voice and ___ move. I tried a change in ___. I kept ___ because ___. One short part of a story. The part you play. A sign that it is your turn. To make one part different.

Pick your role or direct the adult. Use the three short lines with hand cues. Try one pause or move change. Keep your choice. Tell or show why. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use your chosen voice and move. Try the scene with clear turns. Get one notice from a listener. Test one change and log your reason. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Do the same core scene. Keep the role clear when the plan changes. Test two ways to cue the last line. Explain which cue helps the scene most. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

The Keeper says, "My table has moved." The words come fast. The hands stop by the chest. The Keeper then asks, "Can you help?" Are the first words fast or slow? What small hand move did the Keeper use? The Keeper says the same words slowly. One open hand points to an empty spot. There is a short pause. The Keeper then asks, "Can you help?" What has changed in this version? Which version fits your Keeper? Why? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Read all three lines, using a hand cue for each turn. Repeat the last Keeper line with no pause, then with one short pause. Say: I keep the pause because the new choice is clear. Ask the pupil to cue the adult's three turns and confirm the pace. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Develop a character with voice and movement. I can use my chosen voice and move. I can try one helpful change. I can log what I kept and why. scene: One short part of a story. role: The part you play. cue: A sign that it is your turn. change: To make one part different. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can test a drama or sound skill and choose a goal. I can try two versions of one skill. I can explain a choice for a short piece. I can set a small practice goal. Choose drama or quiet original sound. You may perform, direct or work seated. Our invented story is The changed table. Watch or hear two versions of a short line or beat. Which has a pause? What difference do you notice? Explore the two original example cards. Drama uses a line, pause and move. Sound uses beats, a gap and a pace change. Choose one skill to test. Pick one shared skill: pause, pace or a turn cue. Try version A and version B. Ask: Which fits our idea? Give a reason based on what changed. Choose drama or an original quiet sound pattern. Pick one skill to practise. Try two versions. Keep a short trial note. Choose the version that fits your idea. Set one small goal for next lesson. Share one short trial with a chosen listener. Listener: I notice ___. Maker: I chose ___ because ___. Store your plan for Wednesday. Log the art form and skill you tried. Keep your two real versions and reason. Write, say or show your practice goal. Record any support you used. Something you can improve with practice. How fast words, moves or beats happen. A short planned silence or still point. A sign for a performer to start or stop.

Choose drama or quiet sound with an adult. Try a one-count and a two-count gap. Point to the version you want to keep. Say or show why and pick one practice goal. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Choose one skill in drama or original sound. Keep other features the same and test two versions. Get one notice from a listener and choose a version. Record a reason and a small goal for lesson two. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same core task. Set a goal that can be checked in two runs. Ask for feedback on that skill and explain your choice. Optional next level: plan who will hear your short piece and what you want to learn from them. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

The Keeper plans to work at a table. It has moved. The performer says, "The table has moved," pauses for one count, then says, "I can ask for help." One open hand shows the empty space. Where does the performer pause? How could the pause help the audience follow the change? A sound maker creates four soft steady finger taps, one silent count, two slower taps, then four steady taps. The maker says the break marks a plan changing. This is a new class pattern with no tune or words from another work. Which part breaks the first pattern? How could you change the gap or pace to show your own idea? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Read the Keeper line, using a one-count pause before the help line. Repeat with a two-count pause, keeping words and volume the same. Show four soft taps, a two-count gap and four soft taps; silent hand pulses can replace taps. State a small goal: hold the chosen gap in two runs. Ask a pupil to direct the next version. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Set a specific skill goal for two rehearsal runs. Decide who could listen and what feedback you want on that skill. Explain why that audience can help. You can speak, sketch or write. Keep your own goal, two actual trials and audience plan. Record feedback only when it has really happened; a plan is labelled as a plan.

I can practise a chosen skill, use feedback and show a refined piece. I can check my skill goal in two runs. I can test one change after feedback. I can record my choice and next step. Find your real trial note and goal. Choose perform, direct or a silent route. Use the same made-up change story. State or point to your skill goal. Show the chosen cue or pause once. Ask a partner to watch that feature. Watch a short first run. Hear one useful notice. See one change and a second run. How can we check the skill? Try the shared piece once. Listener names the chosen skill. Choose one change and repeat. Check what really happened. Rehearse your drama or original sound piece. Check the skill in two real runs. Get one useful notice. Test one change, or explain why you keep it. Share a short final version with a chosen listener. Share your final short version or direct it. Listener: I notice ___. Maker: I changed or kept ___ because ___. Put plans and real notes in order. Log your two real runs and feedback. Say what you changed or kept, and why. Mark goal met, partly met or next time. Choose one next step for next week's story. To practise a piece before sharing it. A useful notice from a listener or viewer. To make a small change for a clear purpose. A sign to start, pause or stop.

Find or make one small skill goal. Direct or try two short runs with an adult. Hear one notice and choose a change. Confirm a real note of what happened. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use your chosen drama or sound route. Check your goal in two actual runs. Test one change after focused feedback. Log the result, reason and next step. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same core rehearsal and log. Compare the first and refined version in detail. Explain how your skill choice helps the intended audience. Optional next level: lead a short feedback turn and record what you learned from the actual exchange. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Show a brief first run, starting the return before the agreed cue. Listener says: I notice the return began before the cue. Show a clearer hand cue. Repeat and check what happened. Count the real successful run only. Say: That is one success. My goal asks for two; I need one more real run or an honest next step. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Compare two runs of your scene or beat. What got clearer? Which change helped? Say what you kept and why. Set one small skill goal and a way to check it. Keep a note of both runs and your own part. Add the real feedback, your choice and reason. Add your next skill goal.
